name: Brachydactyly type A4

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Brachydactyly Type A4

criteria.description: Shortening or hypoplasia of the distal phalanges of the fingers
Shortening or absence of the middle phalanges of the 2nd to 5th digits
Radiographic evidence of brachydactyly affecting distal and middle phalanges
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
No associated systemic malformations or syndromic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of shortening or hypoplasia of distal and middle phalanges confirmed radiographically in at least two digits, with or without positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may assist but is not always available.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Short middle phalanx of the 5th finger
Shortening of all middle phalanges of the toes
Short middle phalanx of the 2nd finger

common.symptomName: Symphalangism affecting the phalanges of the hand

imaging: Radiographs showing shortening or absence of middle and distal phalanges of fingers
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with phalangeal development (e.g., IHH gene mutations reported in some cases)
other: Clinical examination revealing symmetrical brachydactyly without systemic involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant shortening of middle phalanges of index and middle fingers
Shortening of middle phalanges with metacarpal involvement
Presence of hyperphalangy and variable thumb involvement

redFlags: Presence of systemic malformations suggesting syndromic brachydactyly
Progressive joint contractures or deformities beyond typical presentation
Developmental delay or neurological symptoms indicating broader genetic syndrome
references: Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. 1978.
